newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end lower on poor results.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end lower on poor results.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly lower on Monday, dragged down by firms which have announced poor annual results for 1996, brokers said.
The foreign currency B share index lost 0.10 points or 0.06 percent to end at 176.54 on turnover of HK$273.8 million, compared with HK$144.9 million on Friday.
But losses were offset by demand for blue-chips such as television maker Konka and Guangdong Power, analysts said.
"Today's market was hurt by weak earnings posted by Shenzhen SEZ Real Estate and Baoshi," an analyst with China Southern Securities said.
SEZ Real Estate, a major property firm listed on Shenzhen's B share market, plunged 9.96 percent to end at HK$4.07.
Over the weekend, the company posted a net loss of 26.34 million yuan for 1996 based on international accounting standards.
Based on Chinese standards, the company posted a net profit of 1.70 million yuan for 1996, down from 392.41 million yuan for 1995.
Brokers said they expected SEZ Real Estate to continue to fall in the coming sessions in light of the weak earnings.
Despite today's slight decline in the index, optimism about the market should prevail in May, analysts said.
"The B share market is accumulating momentum to test the 200-point level next month after the end of the 1996 annual reporting season," the China Southern analyst said.
"Many investors believe listed companies are likely to show some improvement in their 1997 interim earnings due to China's improving economy," the analyst said.
"Expected strong debuts by several new B share listings in May are likely to boost market sentiment," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Nanjing Posts & Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd and Sanonda Co Ltd have said they would offer and list 100 million B shares each in Shenzhen in May.
"Nanjing Posts and Sanonda have solid earnings records and are expected to generate strong buying interest," the J&A analyst said.
Konka was the most actively traded stock on Monday and put on HK$0.76 to HK$11.76 on volume of 3.80 million shares.
The A share index edged up 4.40 points or 0.91 percent to close at 488.25 on turnover of 17.7 billion yuan compared with 17.8 billion yuan in the previous session.
